newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER ON MAJOR UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER ON MAJOR UNITS.

text.p: Buying pressure on the interbank market drove the Zimbabwe dollar to end Friday's trading session softer on the key U.S. dollar, sterling and the rand.

Foreign exchange dealers said at one time the local unit eased to 11.2850/2950 against the U.S. dollar from 11.2750/2850 at Thursday's close, but some export receipt inflows pulled it back slightly to end Friday at 11.2800/2900.
"There was a lot of buying, some people were covering their positions even ahead of the Independence Day holiday (next Friday)," one dealer said.
"The central bank didn't intervene, they were sitting on the sidelines watching," he added.

On the crosses, the local unit was indicated at 18.3210/3490 on sterling from 18.2850/3300 and at 2.5310/5350 on the rand versus 2.5266/5340 but was quoted firmer on the mark at 6.5440/5520 from 6.5655/5800.
